newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BROLIN IN REPORTED QUIT THREAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BROLIN IN REPORTED QUIT THREAT.

text.p: Unsettled Swedish international Tomas Brolin has threatened to retire over a dispute with his English premier league club Leeds.
Brolin was signed from Parma in a 4.5 million pounds ($7 million) deal nearly a year ago, but has been on loan recently to FC Zurich.
New Leeds manager George Graham, beset by injuries, insisted that he must return from Zurich so that his fitness could be assessed.
Brolin initially refused to return but changed his mind when Leeds threatened to ask FIFA to impose a worldwide ban on him.
Leeds club solicitor Peter McCormack, speaking on the clubcall service, said: "His parting words were that, unless we gave in, he would retire from football for ever."
Brolin's agent Lars Petersen met McCormack in his Leeds offices on Tuesday to discuss the player's situation.
McCormack said: "Tomas feels he's better off in Switzerland with Zurich for another two months. Then, in December, if he feels right, he would contemplate coming back to join Leeds.
"We made our position clear, which was that his loan agreement with Zurich finished over a week ago and he had a legal obligation to be in this country."
Brolin told the Swedish news agency TT after talks with manager Graham that he had not been able to reach an agreement.
"I have had discussions with George Graham and there's a deadlock. He wants me to come back and I'm not going to," the striker said.
